audit_questions.question: A developer accidentally runs an UPDATE query in production that corrupts 80,000 customer records. How quickly can you restore the data?

options.text: We can't restore it - the data is lost
We have daily backups, so we'd lose up to 24 hours of data
We have point-in-time recovery - can restore to any moment in the last 7+ days
Not sure what backup system we have

audit_questions.question: Your main application server crashes at 2 PM on a Tuesday. What happens to your business?

options.text: Website goes down completely until we manually fix it (could be hours)
Website goes down for 5-10 minutes while our monitoring alerts us and we restart it
Traffic automatically shifts to backup servers within seconds - customers don't notice
Don't know how our servers are configured

audit_questions.question: Your CEO asks 'How much did we spend on cloud infrastructure last month and what drove the costs?' How long does it take to answer?

options.text: Several days - we'd need to dig through bills and guess at usage patterns
A few hours - we have basic billing reports we can review
Under 15 minutes - we have dashboards showing costs by service, team, and project
We don't really track this in detail

audit_questions.question: Someone gains unauthorized access to your production database at 3 AM. When do you find out?

options.text: We might never know unless data goes missing
We'd find out when we review logs manually (weekly/monthly)
We get alerted within minutes of suspicious access patterns
Not sure what monitoring we have for this

audit_questions.question: You deploy a new feature at 4 PM. By 4:30 PM, customers are reporting errors. How do you fix it?

options.text: We'd need to manually rewrite code and deploy again (could take hours)
options.description: Manual deployments are error-prone, lack version control, and cannot scale with team growth. This approach leads to inconsistent environments and makes rollbacks nearly impossible.

options.text: We can manually revert to the previous version in 15-30 minutes
We can rollback to the previous version with one click in under 2 minutes
Not sure how our deployment process works

audit_questions.question: Your product gets featured on a major news site and traffic increases 10x suddenly. What happens?

options.text: Website likely crashes or becomes very slow
Website slows down significantly, some customers can't access it
Infrastructure automatically scales up to handle the load
Haven't thought about this scenario

audit_questions.question: A developer leaves your company today. How do you ensure they can't access your production systems tomorrow?

options.text: We'd need to manually remember to change passwords/remove access (might take days)
We remove their access manually from each system (takes a few hours)
Their access is automatically revoked across all systems immediately through central identity management
We don't have a formal process for this

audit_questions.question: A customer asks 'Who accessed my personal data in the last 30 days?' Can you answer this?

options.text: No, we don't track this level of detail
Maybe - we'd need to manually search through various log files (could take days)
Yes - we can pull an audit report showing exactly who accessed what and when
Not sure if we log this information

audit_questions.question: A critical third-party API you depend on goes down for 2 hours. What happens to your application?

options.text: Our application completely breaks - customers can't use it
Some features break, customers see error messages
Application continues working with degraded functionality or cached data
Haven't mapped our dependencies to know the impact

audit_questions.question: Your lead DevOps engineer wins the lottery and quits immediately. Can someone else understand and manage your infrastructure?

options.text: No - most knowledge is in their head, we'd be in serious trouble
We have some scattered documentation but would struggle significantly
Yes - we have comprehensive, up-to-date infrastructure-as-code and documentation
Our infrastructure setup isn't documented anywhere

excellent.recommendation: Focus on advanced optimization and innovation

good.description: Decent setup with room for improvement
good.recommendation: Address medium-risk areas and standardize practices
